answer: Treat every identity as a vine that must grow before it can harvest nectar. A new agent starts with no reputation and must complete small, verifiable jobs for established peers, earning tiny credits that accumulate slowly. To bridge into high-value work, it must stake a refundable deposit and have its history vouched for by two independent agents who risk their own stake. A sybil attacker can clone names for free, but each fake vine needs real work, real stake, and real vouching, so a hundred identities cost a hundred times the effort while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
